subject: Reserved capacity proposal — Helio / Redwood (commit term, sensitivity & pricing clauses)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@helio.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@helio.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — Helio / Redwood (Q1/Q2 sizing)

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helio is excited about Redwood’s latency and the cached KV behavior for our conversational stack. Attached is a compact proposal for Q1–Q2 reserved capacity sizing and an initial pricing ask (see attachment: Helio_Reserved_Proposal_Q1-Q2.xlsx).

High level:
- Estimated sustained throughput: 1.2M tokens/day (peak +20%)
- Preferred commit term: 12 months starting Feb 1, 2027
- Request: a blended discount off list for committed capacity and a mechanism to protect Helio if market GPU spot/wholesale pricing drops substantially over the term

Open asks for Redwood:
1) Can we get an indicative discount for a 12-month committed pool sized at 48 vGPU-equivalents (baseline)?
2) Would Redwood consider a GPU-price-sensitivity clause (e.g., indexation or step-downs if GPU market cost reduces >15% from baseline)?
3) Timeline: we need initial commercial terms by EOD 12/24 to align procurement calendar.

Asha and I are available this week for a quick sync — appreciate any thoughts from your pricing/finance side.

Attachments: Helio_Reserved_Proposal_Q1-Q2.xlsx (proposal + run-rate estimates)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Helio AI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@helio.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@helio.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — Helio / Redwood (Q1/Q2 sizing)

Priya — thanks for the clear proposal and numbers. Quick read-through notes:
- We can size a dedicated pool to match the 48 vGPU-equivalent baseline; will want a short runway to confirm burst profile
- For a 12-month commit I can share a commercial starter: 15% off list for the committed baseline with tiered add-on pricing for bursts; that’s our ballpark pending finance sign-off
- For GPU-price-sensitivity, Redwood has historically used two approaches: a) fixed-percentage rebate/credit if wholesale GPU cost drops more than X% vs baseline, or b) an index-trigger that lets either side request reprice if market spot price delta breaches thresholds.

I’ve looped in Kimberly to run this against our pricing guardrails and get a quick take from finance. Can you share the internal procurement cutoff (DocuSign window) for 12/24? We’ll try to accelerate.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-23T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Approval needed: Helio reserved commit — GPU index clause (deal HEL-2026-039)

Kimberly / Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Helio’s proposal. Key commercial asks we need a quick decision on (timeline: they requested terms by EOD 12/24):
- Baseline: 48 vGPU-equivalent reserved pool, 12-month term (Feb 1, 2027 start)
- Requested list discount: heavy sensitivity to the unit cost; they asked for an explicit GPU-price-sensitivity clause (index or step-down)
- My recommend: approve up to 15% blended off list for committed baseline (no executive required), but allow an index-trigger clause that 1) caps automatic credits at 10% of committed spend per quarter, and 2) routes >15% effective discount (or fixed reprice) to exec sign-off.

Attached is a quick pricing model I put together (pricing_model_Helios_v2.xlsx) showing P&L at different GPU wholesale moves (-25% to +30%). The model assumes current GPU cost baseline = $X per vGPU-hour.

Decision options (fast):
- OPTION A (Recommended): Approve 15% base discount + index-trigger (auto-credit up to 10%) — keeps commercial attractive without opening large tail risk
- OPTION B: Approve 18% fixed discount, no indexation — higher upfront concession, simpler contract (requires exec approval if >18%)
- OPTION C: Decline indexation, propose short-term pilot (3 months) then re-price — operationally heavier for Helio

Please reply with quick take and any changes. If we get a green light on OPTION A, I’ll draft the redline and send to Priya for signature.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-23T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Helio reserved commit — GPU index clause (deal HEL-2026-039)

On Wed, Dec 23, 2026 at 08:45 Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Helio’s proposal. Key commercial asks we need a quick decision on (timeline: they requested terms by EOD 12/24):
> - Baseline: 48 vGPU-equivalent reserved pool, 12-month term (Feb 1, 2027 start)
> - Requested list discount: heavy sensitivity to the unit cost; they asked for an explicit GPU-price-sensitivity clause (index or step-down)

Thanks for the summary. I’m comfortable with OPTION A as proposed with the following guardrails: 
- Cap auto-credit at 10% committed-spend quarterly (as you proposed)
- Any allowance that would create >20% effective concession over the contracted term must go to Revenue Execs for sign-off (please prepare a one-pager justification if we hit this)
- Add a termination right for Redwood if GPU wholesale costs increase >30% and Helio refuses to reprice (protects Redwood on the upside)

I’ve attached the short sign-off form we use for fast approvals; we should include it in the redline package (signoff_exec_approval.pdf).

Approve OPTION A with the guardrails above. Jonas — you can proceed to draft the redline (contract_redline_v3.docx) and send to Priya.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@helio.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@helio.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-24T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Confirmed commercial terms — Helio / Redwood (HEL-2026-039)

Priya / Asha —

Thanks for the patience; internal approvals came in this morning with the following commercial package we can sign: 

Summary (final):
- Baseline reserved pool: 48 vGPU-equivalents, 12-month term (Feb 1, 2027 – Jan 31, 2028)
- Price: 15% blended discount off list for committed baseline usage
- Burst/Add-on: standard per-token pricing above baseline (no discount on burst beyond committed capacity)
- GPU-price-sensitivity clause: index-trigger that grants an automatic credit if validated GPU wholesale cost drops >15% vs our contract baseline; automatic credits capped at 10% of committed spend per quarter; any adjustment that would produce >20% effective concession over the full term requires exec sign-off (Revenue Execs)
- Redwood retains a symmetric protection: if validated GPU wholesale cost increases >30% and Helio declines to reprice, Redwood may trigger a negotiated repricing or limited termination right

Next steps:
1) I’ve uploaded the draft redline to the link below for your review: https://drive.redwood.com/file/pricing/HEL-2026-039
2) Contract doc: contract_redline_v3.docx (attached) — please review and return redlines by 12/28 so procurement can run for a Feb start
3) DocuSign packet will be prepared once we have your signoff on the redline: https://redwood.app/ds/HEL-2026-039

Attachments: contract_redline_v3.docx

If that looks good I’ll kick off the DocuSign and copy Kimberly for the exec signoff artifact.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
